questions.q: In static batching, what happens if one request in the batch finishes much earlier than the others?
options: It immediately returns its result while the rest of the batch keeps running
It is dropped from the batch and re-queued
The whole batch still finishes together, because the batch runs and completes as one unit
The batch automatically splits into two smaller batches
questions.explain: Static batching treats the batch as a single unit — it starts and finishes together, so an early-finishing request still waits for the slowest member of the batch.

questions.q: What are the two knobs every dynamic batcher exposes?
options: GPU temperature and fan speed
Max batch size and max queue delay
Model precision and context length
Tokenizer version and vocabulary size
questions.explain: Dynamic batchers let you tune a ceiling on batch size (max batch size) and how long to wait for more requests to arrive before running (max queue delay).

questions.q: What effect does a longer max queue delay typically have?
options: It lowers throughput and lowers latency at the same time
It has no effect on either metric
It tends to raise throughput (bigger batches) at the cost of higher latency for early-arriving requests
It only affects tokenization speed
questions.explain: A longer queue delay gives more requests a chance to join the batch, raising throughput, but it makes requests that arrived early wait longer before the batch runs.

questions.q: Why is static or basic dynamic batching a poor fit for LLM text generation specifically?
options: LLMs cannot be batched at all
Requests in the same batch finish generating at very different times (one may need 20 tokens, another 2,000), so the whole batch waits on the slowest
LLM tokenizers are incompatible with batching
GPUs cannot process more than one LLM request simultaneously
questions.explain: Because LLM output lengths vary widely per request, treating a batch as a single start-to-finish unit means short requests are stuck waiting for the longest one to finish.

questions.q: What does continuous batching change compared to dynamic batching?
options: It removes the need for a tokenizer
It lets individual requests join and leave the batch at each decode step, instead of treating the whole batch as one unit
It only works for static, offline workloads
It eliminates the need for a GPU
questions.explain: Continuous batching operates at the granularity of a single generated token: as soon as one request finishes, its GPU slot is handed to a new request immediately, rather than waiting for the whole batch to complete.
